holidays.name: National Tater Tot Day
holidays.description: A salute to the crispy, bite-sized golden barrels of shredded potato that have been rescuing lunch trays and appetizer platters for decades. Dip them, pile them into a casserole, or eat them straight from the bag.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food observance. Tater Tots were invented in 1953 by brothers F. Nephi and Golden Grigg, who founded Ore-Ida. They made the snack from leftover potato scraps.
holidays.funFact: The Grigg brothers reportedly made Tater Tots from potato trimmings that would otherwise have been thrown away. The snack went on to sell millions of pounds a year.

holidays.name: National Hedgehog Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the spiky, snuffly, insect-munching hedgehog. It shares the date with Groundhog Day, so it gives another small mammal a turn in the spotlight.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance, usually linked to Groundhog Day. The date is a nod to the old European weather folklore that came before the groundhog tradition.
holidays.funFact: European folklore held that a badger or a hedgehog could predict the weather on Candlemas. German immigrants later swapped in the groundhog in Pennsylvania.

holidays.name: Crêpe Day (Candlemas)
holidays.description: In France, February 2 is la Chandeleur, the day for flipping thin pancakes and eating them with sweet toppings. It is a delicious excuse to practice your pan-tossing skills.
holidays.origin: La Chandeleur is the French name for Candlemas, a Christian feast held 40 days after Christmas. Its round, golden crêpes came to symbolize the sun and the return of spring.
holidays.funFact: A French tradition says to flip a crêpe with your writing hand while holding a coin in the other. Doing it successfully is said to bring a year of prosperity.
